title: Residential Termite Control
intro: Make room for living. Keep termites out. Get an inspection-led treatment plan for your home, wooden furniture and the hidden places that need attention.
heroAlt: Termite-care specialist inspecting a timber doorway at a garden villa
definition: Residential termite control starts with inspecting your home for termite activity, vulnerable timber and possible entry routes. The findings guide a treatment plan for affected and accessible areas, followed by practical advice on preparation, moisture management and ongoing checks.
benefitTitle: 6 reasons to give your home a closer look
benefits: Early identification
Have suspicious termite signs assessed through a careful inspection of accessible areas.
Timber attention
Check doors, frames, cabinets and skirting for visible damage or termite activity.
Targeted treatment
Focus treatment on accessible areas identified during a careful inspection of activity.
A plan for your home
Consider your home's layout, access and daily routine when planning treatment visits.
Clear preparation
Understand the preparation, access and re-entry instructions for your agreed treatment visit.
Practical aftercare
Understand which signs to monitor and when to arrange follow-up after treatment.
processIntro: From the first signs to a considered plan for your home.
steps: Tell us what you have noticed. We check accessible timber, wall-floor junctions and moisture-prone areas.
Review visible termite signs and the places that may need closer attention.
Discuss the proposed method, access, preparation and quotation before work begins.
Carry out the planned work with attention to your home’s finishes and occupied spaces.
Share aftercare guidance and confirm any agreed monitoring or warranty terms.

faqs.question: What signs should I look for at home?
faqs.answer: Mud tubes, discarded wings, damaged timber or wood that sounds hollow can justify an inspection. These signs can have other causes, so an assessment helps establish what is happening.

faqs.question: Will my furniture need treatment?
faqs.answer: We inspect accessible furniture and fixed woodwork, then explain which items need attention. The recommendation depends on the material, activity and access.

faqs.question: Do I need to leave home during treatment?
faqs.answer: Preparation and re-entry requirements depend on the method and products selected. Our team will explain the instructions for your property before the visit.

faqs.question: How do I arrange a home inspection?
faqs.answer: Share your city, property type and any signs you have noticed using the form below. The team will confirm availability and discuss a suitable time.

title: Commercial Termite Control
intro: Protect your premises. Keep business moving. Plan termite inspections and treatment around your building, operating hours and access requirements.
heroAlt: Termite-care specialist inspecting a timber entrance frame outside a modern glass office building
definition: Commercial termite control brings property assessment, treatment planning and service reporting together for business premises. We review accessible timber, structural junctions and areas of concern, then propose work that considers the building’s use, access and operating schedule.
benefitTitle: 6 ways a planned approach supports your business
benefits: Premises assessment
Review accessible timber, building junctions and areas of concern across your premises.
Timber protection
Inspect fittings, fixtures and joinery to identify visible signs of termite activity.
Flexible planning
Discuss suitable inspection and treatment timings around your staff and business operations.
Site-specific scope
Match treatment plans to your building layout, access requirements and daily operations.
Service records
Keep inspection notes, agreed treatment areas and visit details organised together clearly.
Continuing care
Discuss follow-up inspections and maintenance options suited to your premises and needs.
processIntro: An organised service plan for your people, premises and operations.
steps: Review property use, affected areas, access restrictions and operating hours with your site contact.
Check accessible timber, building junctions and visible signs of termite activity.
Agree the scope, method, preparation and timing for each area of the building.
Complete the agreed treatment in coordination with the responsible site team.
Provide service information and discuss follow-up or an ongoing maintenance plan.

faqs.question: Can work be planned around business hours?
faqs.answer: Share your operating schedule and access requirements. We will discuss available appointments and whether the proposed treatment can be staged around your operations.

faqs.question: Do you inspect large or multi-area properties?
faqs.answer: We can discuss the size and layout of your premises and plan an assessment. Larger or complex sites may need a coordinated inspection with a facilities representative.

faqs.question: Will we receive service documentation?
faqs.answer: The agreed service scope and records are discussed before work starts. Tell us about any reporting requirements so the team can confirm what can be provided.

faqs.question: Can we arrange ongoing maintenance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ask about an annual maintenance plan. Visit frequency, included areas and treatment terms are agreed for the property.

title: Pre-Construction Termite Treatment
intro: Protect your new building from termite infestation with professional pre-construction anti-termite treatment.
heroAlt: Site engineer reviewing plans beside a concrete building under construction
definition: Pre-construction anti-termite treatment is a preventive process carried out during construction to help protect your building from subterranean termites. It involves applying a termiticide to the soil at the right stages of construction.
benefitTitle: 6 Reasons to Protect Your Building Before Construction Is Completed
benefits: Foundation Protection
Treat exposed foundation soil before building work covers these important access points.
Under-floor Protection
Plan soil treatment beneath floors while the plinth filling remains fully accessible.
Preventive Approach
Include termite prevention in your construction schedule before the building takes shape.
Entry-Point Attention
Identify pipe routes and service junctions that need attention during planned treatment.
Suitable for All Projects
Discuss soil treatment for homes, apartments, offices and other planned building projects.
Planned Application
Coordinate treatment visits with your builder around the relevant stages of construction.
processIntro: A systematic approach to create a strong termite protection barrier.
steps: Treat the bottom and sides of foundation trenches.
Cover pipe and other entry points.

faqs.question: What is pre-construction termite treatment?
faqs.answer: Pre-construction anti-termite treatment is a preventive process carried out during construction to help protect your building from subterranean termites. It involves applying a termiticide to the soil at the right stages of construction.

faqs.question: When should treatment be done?
faqs.answer: Treatment is planned at the right stages of construction, including foundation trenches, backfill soil, plinth filling, service entries and the external perimeter. Contact our team before these areas are covered.

faqs.question: Is it necessary for new buildings?
faqs.answer: New buildings can also be vulnerable to subterranean termites. Pre-construction treatment helps create a protective barrier beneath and around the building while the soil is accessible.

title: Post-Construction Termite Treatment
intro: An existing building. A fresh layer of protection. Address termite activity around floors, walls and vulnerable woodwork with a property-specific treatment plan.
heroAlt: Protected technician applying precision treatment at a finished home’s wall-floor junction
definition: Post-construction treatment addresses termite activity in completed or occupied buildings. After an inspection, suitable treatment may include targeted drilling and injection at accessible junctions, attention to affected woodwork and measures to address likely entry routes.
benefitTitle: 6 reasons to act on signs in an existing building
benefits: Find the activity
Inspect visible termite signs and accessible timber to understand the current activity.
Address entry routes
Review accessible floor and wall junctions to identify possible termite entry routes.
Targeted application
Select suitable treatment methods for the affected areas identified during your inspection.
Existing-building care
Plan treatment access around existing finishes, occupied rooms and your daily routine.
Clear scope of work
Understand the proposed treatment method, preparation and agreed areas before work begins.
Aftercare guidance
Understand aftercare guidance and which changes may need attention following your treatment.
processIntro: Find the signs. Reach suitable treatment points. Plan the next step.
steps: Check accessible timber, mud tubes and the junctions where activity has been noticed.
Review entry routes, building finishes and the treatment access available.
Explain the proposed work, including drilling and injection where suitable, before treatment starts.
Treat the agreed areas and address affected woodwork as set out in your service plan.
Explain preparation for re-use, monitoring and any agreed follow-up or warranty terms.

faqs.question: Will treatment involve drilling?
faqs.answer: Drilling and injection may be recommended where suitable access is needed. The team will explain the proposed locations, method and finishing arrangements after the inspection.

faqs.question: Can an occupied property be treated?
faqs.answer: The plan considers how the building is used and which areas are accessible. Preparation, access and re-entry instructions will be explained for the selected treatment.

faqs.question: Is damaged wood restored by treatment?
faqs.answer: Treatment addresses termite activity; it does not restore damaged timber. Any repair or replacement needs to be assessed separately.

faqs.question: What if I have already had termite treatment?
faqs.answer: Share the previous service details and any new signs you have noticed. We will assess the current situation before recommending further work.

title: Annual Maintenance Contract
intro: Protection needs attention, not guesswork. Keep termite care on the calendar with scheduled inspections, service records and support under an agreed plan.
heroAlt: Specialist recording a scheduled timber inspection on a tablet beside a garden veranda
definitionTitle: What is a termite maintenance contract?
definition: An annual maintenance contract, or AMC, is an agreed plan for regular termite inspections, monitoring and support. The inspection frequency, covered areas, included treatments and re-treatment terms are set out for your property before the contract starts.
benefitTitle: 6 reasons to keep termite care on your calendar
benefits: Scheduled inspections
Arrange regular inspection visits around your property access and agreed service schedule.
Continuing attention
Monitor areas of previous concern and discuss new signs between scheduled visits.
A property-specific plan
Agree inspection areas, visit frequency and treatment inclusions before your plan begins.
Clear service records
Keep inspection notes, visit details and agreed service records organised together clearly.
Prevention guidance
Discuss moisture, maintenance and property conditions that may need attention between visits.
Defined support
Understand your agreed plan, included care and support available between scheduled visits.
processTitle: How your annual maintenance plan works
processIntro: A clear agreement. Regular checks. Care that continues.
steps: Inspect accessible areas and review any termite history or previous treatment.
Confirm covered areas, visit frequency, treatment inclusions and the contract period.
Arrange the agreed checks and coordinate access with your household or site team.
Document observations and carry out any work included under your agreement.
Discuss changes to the property, ongoing care needs and renewal options before the plan ends.

faqs.question: How many inspections are included?
faqs.answer: The visit frequency is agreed for your property and stated in the contract. Ask the team to confirm the schedule, covered areas and access requirements before signing.

faqs.question: Does an AMC include every type of treatment?
faqs.answer: Coverage depends on the agreement. Inspection, preventive work, re-treatment and exclusions should be reviewed with the team so you know exactly what is included.

faqs.question: Can I take an AMC after an earlier treatment?
faqs.answer: Share your previous treatment details and current concerns. An initial assessment helps us propose a suitable maintenance scope for your property.

faqs.question: Is renewal automatic?
faqs.answer: Renewal arrangements depend on the contract you agree to. The team can explain the duration, expiry and renewal process before your plan starts.
